title: "Supplementary Studies"
author: "Przemek Marcowski"
---

This notebook holds the supplementary experiments and the analyses that span
experiments: the effort-manipulation validation samples (Experiments S1 and
S2), the two control studies on the baseline relation between price and liking
(Experiments S3 and S4), the foraging-experience study (Experiment S5), the
waiting study (Experiment S6), the pooled comparison of performed
and observed effort, the participant rating profiles across experiments, the
responses to the Instrumentality items, the post-experiment task load
across experiments, and two exploratory moderation analyses of Experiment 4
(object liking and rating response time). The sections run from the
manipulation, through the baseline controls and the foraging and waiting
experiments, to the analyses that span experiments and the two exploratory
analyses of Experiment 4, and end with a summary table. Prepared data are read
from each study's `data/` directory. The analyses of Experiment S7, the
post-effort target reveal, stay with Experiment 4 in `main.qmd`, and the
task-by-task detail of the cognitive experiment stays with Experiment 5; the
two appraisal sections list Experiment S7 and the two tasks of Experiment 5 as
separate samples.

| Section | Reported as | Figures and tables |
|---|---|---|
| Experiments S1 and S2: Effort Manipulation Validation | Supplemental Material, Experiments S1 and S2 | S2, S3 |
| Experiment S3: Price and Liking at Baseline | Supplemental Material, Experiment S3 | S4 |
| Experiment S4: Explicit Price and Liking | Supplemental Material, Experiment S4 | S5 |
| Experiment S5: Foraging Experience | Supplemental Material, Experiment S5 | S11 |
| Experiment S6: Waiting | Supplemental Material, Experiment S6 | S14 |
| Performed vs Observed Effort | Supplemental Material, Comparative Analysis: Performed vs. Observed Effort | S10 |
| Rating Profiles Across Experiments | Supplemental Material, Participant Rating Profiles | S9 |
| Instrumentality Across Experiments | Supplemental Material, Perceived Instrumentality and Meaning of Effort | Table S1 |
| Post-Experiment Task Load Across Experiments | Supplemental Material, Post-Experiment Task Load | Table S2 |
| Object Liking and the Effects of Effort | Supplemental Material, Object Liking and the Effects of Effort | — |
| Rating Response Time and the Effects of Effort | Supplemental Material, Rating Response Time and the Effects of Effort | — |

```{r setup, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(afex)
library(emmeans)
library(here)

here::i_am("analysis/supplementary.qmd")
set.seed(42)
emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 2e+5)

source(here("R/functions.R"))
```

# Experiments S1 and S2: Effort Manipulation Validation

Two standalone validation samples test whether the physical effort
manipulations produce graded task-load experiences: a laboratory sample
performing the stepping task and an online sample performing the clicking
task. In both, participants rated NASA-TLX components after each trial, so
task-demand components should rise with effort level while performance
self-assessments need not.

## Experiment S1: Laboratory Stepping

```{r taskload-stepping-data}
taskload_stepping_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/taskload_stepping/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(subjID, sex), as.factor),
    component = factor(component, levels = tlx_components)
  )

n_taskload_stepping <- n_distinct(taskload_stepping_data$subjID)
```

The laboratory validation sample comprises `r n_taskload_stepping`
participants.

```{r taskload-stepping-sample}
taskload_stepping_data %>%
  group_by(subjID) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age), sd_age = sd(age),
    n_male = sum(sex == "Male"), n_female = sum(sex == "Female")
  )
```

One factorial model with effort level and component as fixed effects and a
random intercept per participant tests whether the components respond to
effort differently.

```{r taskload-stepping-omnibus}
taskload_stepping_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * component + (1 | subjID),
  data = taskload_stepping_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(taskload_stepping_omnibus)
```

The linear trend of each component across effort levels gives its slope per
level step.

```{r taskload-stepping-slopes}
taskload_stepping_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * component + (1 | subjID),
  data = taskload_stepping_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

emtrends(taskload_stepping_trend, ~component, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
```

```{r taskload-stepping-plot}
# Cell means with normal-theory 95% CIs on the laboratory 1-5 scale
taskload_stepping_means <- taskload_stepping_data %>%
  group_by(effort_level, component) %>%
  summarize(mean_cl_normal(rating), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(emmean = y, lower.CL = ymin, upper.CL = ymax)

taskload_stepping_plot <- plot_taskload_by_effort(taskload_stepping_means, ylim = c(1, 5))

save_figure(taskload_stepping_plot, "taskload_stepping")
```

# Experiment S3: Price and Liking at Baseline

Participants rated ideographs on both price and liking, with question order
counterbalanced between participants. Within-participant correlations test
whether price and liking judgments track each other at baseline, with no
effort involved. A participant with no rating variance in one condition has
an undefined correlation and drops from the comparison.

```{r price-liking-data}
price_liking_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/price_liking_order/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    cond = factor(cond, levels = c("Liking First", "Price First"))
  )

n_price_liking <- n_distinct(price_liking_data$id)

price_liking_by_id <- price_liking_data %>%
  group_by(id, cond) %>%
  summarize(
    meanL = mean(Liking), meanP = mean(Price),
    sdL = sd(Liking), sdP = sd(Price),
    corl = if (isTRUE(sdL > 0 && sdP > 0)) cor(Liking, Price) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(exclude = is.na(corl))

price_liking_excluded <- unique(price_liking_by_id$id[price_liking_by_id$exclude])
price_liking_by_id <- price_liking_by_id %>% filter(!id %in% price_liking_excluded)
price_liking_analyzed <- price_liking_data %>% filter(!id %in% price_liking_excluded)

n_price_liking_analyzed <- n_distinct(price_liking_analyzed$id)
```

Of `r n_price_liking` participants, `r length(price_liking_excluded)` had no
rating variance in one condition, leaving `r n_price_liking_analyzed` in the
analyses.

The pooled correlation within each order condition, the difference between
the two pooled correlations (Zou's interval, comparing the conditions as
independent groups), and a paired test of the per-participant correlations
across order:

```{r price-liking-correlations}
price_liking_analyzed %>%
  group_by(cond) %>%
  rstatix::cor_test(Liking, Price) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

price_liking_analyzed %>%
  group_by(cond) %>%
  summarize(n = n())

price_liking_split <- price_liking_analyzed %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  split(.$cond)
cocor::cocor(~ Liking + Price | Liking + Price, price_liking_split)

price_liking_by_id %>% rstatix::t_test(corl ~ cond, paired = TRUE)
```

```{r price-liking-plot}
price_liking_scatter <- price_liking_analyzed %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Price, y = Liking)) +
  geom_jitter(shape = 16, size = 0.75, alpha = 0.5, colour = "grey50",
              position = position_jitter(seed = 42)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", fullrange = FALSE, colour = evl_colours[["Teal"]],
              fill = evl_colours[["Teal Light"]]) +
  labs(title = "Relationship Between Price and Liking") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 5, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 5, 1)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, 5.5), ylim = c(0.5, 5.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~cond) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(price_liking_scatter, "price_liking_scatter")
```

# Experiment S4: Explicit Price and Liking

Participants rated liking for items presented with explicit price tags at
small versus large price magnitudes (between subjects), testing whether
stated prices shift liking when no effort is involved. Each survey session
is one participant.

```{r price-magnitude-data}
price_magnitude_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/price_magnitude/data/main.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(id, magnitude), as.factor),
    liking = as.numeric(liking),
    value = factor(value, levels = 1:5)
  )

n_price_magnitude <- n_distinct(price_magnitude_data$id)
```

The sample comprises `r n_price_magnitude` participants.

```{r price-magnitude-omnibus}
price_magnitude_omnibus <- mixed(
  liking ~ magnitude * value + (1 | id),
  data = price_magnitude_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(price_magnitude_omnibus)
```

```{r price-magnitude-plot}
price_magnitude_plot <- price_magnitude_data %>%
  mutate(magnitude = factor(recode(magnitude, "Big" = "Large"), levels = c("Small", "Large"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = liking, group = magnitude)) +
  stat_summary(
    geom = "errorbar", fun.data = mean_cl_normal, colour = evl_colours[["Teal"]],
    width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(fill = magnitude), geom = "point", fun = mean, shape = 21,
    colour = evl_colours[["Teal"]], position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(Small = "white", Large = evl_colours[["Teal"]]),
    name = "Price Magnitude"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "1" = "$1\n$100", "2" = "$2\n$200", "3" = "$3\n$300",
    "4" = "$4\n$400", "5" = "$5\n$500"
  )) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  labs(title = "Explicit Price and Liking", x = "Price", y = "Mean Liking") +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom", panel = c(55, 40))

save_figure(price_magnitude_plot, "price_magnitude_liking")
```

# Experiment S5: Foraging Experience

Participants judged either the liking or the price of items obtained at three
effort levels in a foraging frame (judgment type between subjects), with prior
foraging experience also manipulated between subjects. The question is whether
direct experience of effortful acquisition changes how effort maps onto the two
judgment types.

```{r foraging-data}
foraging_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/foraging/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    type = factor(type, levels = c("Liking", "Value")),
    experience = factor(experience, levels = c("No Experience", "Experience"))
  )

n_foraging <- n_distinct(foraging_data$subjID)
```

The sample comprises `r n_foraging` participants.

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with judgment type, experience, and effort level as fixed
effects carries the dissociation in the judgment-by-effort interaction and its
dependence on experience in the three-way term.

```{r foraging-omnibus}
foraging_omnibus <- mixed(
  value ~ type * experience * effort_level + (1 | subjID),
  data = foraging_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(foraging_omnibus)
```

The effort slope of each judgment type, averaged over experience, and their
difference come from the numeric-effort model.

```{r foraging-slopes}
foraging_trend <- mixed(
  value ~ type * experience * effort_num + (1 | subjID),
  data = foraging_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

foraging_slopes <- emtrends(foraging_trend, ~type, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
foraging_slopes

foraging_slope_diffs <- pairs(foraging_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
foraging_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r foraging-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(foraging_slopes, foraging_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

Experience shifts the level of each judgment type rather than its effort
slope, and the two-level simple effects show the shift.

```{r foraging-experience-effects}
withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(foraging_omnibus, pairwise ~ experience | type,
                             infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt"))
```

```{r foraging-plot}
foraging_means <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(foraging_omnibus, ~ effort_level * type * experience)
)

pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.4)
foraging_plot <- foraging_means %>%
  mutate(
    type = recode(type, "Value" = "Price"),
    experience = recode(experience, "No Experience" = "No", "Experience" = "Yes"),
    point_fill = if_else(experience == "Yes", as.character(type), "Open")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = experience, colour = type)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3, position = pd) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = experience), position = pd) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = point_fill), shape = 21, position = pd) +
  scale_evl(guide = "none", fill = TRUE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(No = "dashed", Yes = "solid")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~type) +
  labs(
    title = "Liking, Price, and Foraging Experience",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating",
    linetype = "Foraging Experience"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom")

show_figure(foraging_plot)
```

## Strategies

Free-text strategy reports were hand-coded into categories, one primary
category per response for the pre-task strategy question and for the
valuation strategy question. The counts and shares are descriptive.

```{r foraging-strategies}
foraging_strategies <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/foraging/data/coded_categories.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

n_foraging_strategies <- nrow(foraging_strategies)

foraging_strategy_long <- foraging_strategies %>%
  transmute(
    q1 = strategyq1_primary_category,
    q2 = strategyq2_primary_category
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "question", values_to = "category") %>%
  mutate(
    question = recode(question, q1 = "Pre-Task Strategy", q2 = "Valuation Strategy"),
    category = str_replace(str_trim(category), " Or ", " or ")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(category), category != "")

foraging_strategy_order <- foraging_strategy_long %>%
  count(category, sort = TRUE) %>%
  pull(category)

foraging_strategy_counts <- foraging_strategy_long %>%
  mutate(category = factor(category, levels = rev(foraging_strategy_order))) %>%
  count(question, category, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(question) %>%
  mutate(pct_in_question = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(pct_total = n / n_foraging_strategies)

foraging_strategy_counts

strategy_dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.85, preserve = "single", reverse = TRUE)
foraging_strategies_plot <- foraging_strategy_counts %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = category, fill = question)) +
  geom_col(position = strategy_dodge, width = 0.8, colour = "black") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * pct_total), group = question),
    position = strategy_dodge, hjust = -0.15
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Pre-Task Strategy" = "white", "Valuation Strategy" = evl_colours[["Teal"]]),
    guide = guide_legend(title = NULL)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Strategy Categories",
    subtitle = "Primary Label; % of Total N",
    x = "Count", y = NULL
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(foraging_strategy_counts$n) * 1.45)) +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom", panel = c(60, 110)) +
  theme(legend.location = "plot")

save_figure(foraging_strategies_plot, "foraging_strategies")
```

# Experiment S6: Waiting

Participants faced a passive forced wait of 10, 20, or 40 s (Low, Medium,
High; within subjects) in place of any effort task, and object preview (object
shown 4 s before the wait versus hidden until the rating screen) is crossed
with rating condition (liking or price), both between subjects. Wait level
stands in for effort magnitude, isolating temporal cost to test whether the
price–liking dissociation seen with effort is driven by how long one waits.
Because the wait doubles with each level (10, 20, 40 s), the per-level slope
reads as the change per doubling of wait time. The analyzed sample excludes
participants without a completed post-survey or with chance-level recognition
memory (d′ ≤ 0). The summed-time cutoff of the effort studies does not apply
here: the wait is program-imposed and identical for everyone, so its duration
cannot indicate whether a participant was engaged, and off-task behavior is
read from focus loss instead.

```{r wait-data}
wait_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/wait/data/main.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value")),
    preview_assignment = factor(preview_assignment, levels = c("nopreview", "preview"))
  )

wait_memory <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/wait/data/memory.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  ) %>%
  filter(id %in% unique(wait_data$id))

n_wait <- n_distinct(wait_data$id)
```

The analyzed sample comprises `r n_wait` participants.

```{r wait-sample}
wait_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(id),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_male = n_distinct(id[gender == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(id[gender == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(id[!gender %in% c("Male", "Female")]),
    n_liking = n_distinct(id[condition == "Liking"]),
    n_value = n_distinct(id[condition == "Value"]),
    n_preview = n_distinct(id[preview_assignment == "preview"]),
    n_nopreview = n_distinct(id[preview_assignment == "nopreview"])
  )
```

## Memory Check

```{r wait-memory}
memory_summary(wait_memory)
```

## Wait Manipulation Check

Realized wait duration should track the assigned wait level, and off-task
focus loss during the wait indexes compliance.

```{r wait-manipulation}
wait_duration <- mixed(
  effort_trial_duration ~ effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = wait_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(wait_duration)

emmeans(wait_duration, ~effort_level, infer = TRUE)

wait_focus <- mixed(
  wait_focus_lost ~ effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = wait_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(wait_focus)
emmeans(wait_focus, ~effort_level, infer = TRUE)
```

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with wait level and rating condition as fixed effects and
a random intercept per participant carries the dissociation in its
interaction.

```{r wait-omnibus}
wait_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = wait_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(wait_omnibus)
```

```{r wait-slopes}
wait_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (1 | id),
  data = wait_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

wait_slopes <- emtrends(wait_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
wait_slopes

wait_slope_diffs <- pairs(wait_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
wait_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r wait-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(wait_slopes, wait_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

```{r wait-plot}
wait_means <- as.data.frame(emmeans(wait_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition))

wait_plot <-
  wait_means %>%
  mutate(condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    Low = "Low\n(10 s)", Medium = "Medium\n(20 s)", High = "High\n(40 s)"
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ratings of Liking and Price",
    subtitle = "Waiting",
    x = "Wait Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(wait_plot, "wait_ratings")
```

## Moderation by Preview

Whether the object was previewed before the wait enters as a third factor.

```{r wait-preview}
wait_preview <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition * preview_assignment + (1 | id),
  data = wait_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(wait_preview)
```

## Moderation by Task Load

The post-task NASA-TLX score enters as a continuous moderator of the
dissociation, and the slopes at lower and higher task load (the mean minus and
plus one SD) show whether waiting dissociates the judgments among participants
who found it demanding, as serial subtraction did.

```{r wait-task-load}
wait_task_load <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition * scale(nasa_tlx) + (1 | id),
  data = wait_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(wait_task_load)

wait_task_load_levels <- mean(wait_data$nasa_tlx) + c(-1, 1) * sd(wait_data$nasa_tlx)

emtrends(
  wait_task_load,
  pairwise ~ condition | nasa_tlx,
  var = "effort_num",
  at = list(nasa_tlx = wait_task_load_levels),
  infer = TRUE
)
```

# Performed vs Observed Effort

Pooling the laboratory stepping study (performed effort) with the online
observation study (observed effort) tests whether the effort-rating patterns
require performing the effort oneself. Only the liking and price rating
conditions common to both studies enter the pooled frame.

```{r performed-observed-data}
performed_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/stepping/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(id = subjID, rt = ratingRT, gender = sex, nasa_tlx = raw_overall,
         effort_steps = effort_trials, everything()) %>%
  mutate(perspective = "Perform")

observed_pooled_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/observed/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(perspective = "Observe", age = as.numeric(age))

performed_observed_data <-
  bind_rows(performed_data, observed_pooled_data) %>%
  select(
    -any_of(c("experiment_id", "steps_correct", "effort_time")),
    -starts_with("frustration_"), -starts_with("rel_")
  ) %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("Liking", "Value")) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(id, gender), as.factor),
    perspective = factor(perspective, levels = c("Perform", "Observe")),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

n_performed_observed <- n_distinct(performed_observed_data$id)
```

The pooled frame holds `r n_performed_observed` participants across the two
studies.

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with effort level, rating condition, and perspective as
fixed effects carries the question in its condition-by-perspective and
three-way terms.

```{r performed-observed-omnibus}
performed_observed_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition * perspective + (1 | id),
  data = performed_observed_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(performed_observed_omnibus)

performed_observed_means <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(performed_observed_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition * perspective)
)
```

The effort slope of each judgment within each perspective, the slope
difference within each perspective, and the contrast between the two slope
differences locate where performing the effort matters.

```{r performed-observed-slopes}
performed_observed_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition * perspective + (1 | id),
  data = performed_observed_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

performed_observed_slopes <- emtrends(
  performed_observed_trend, ~ condition | perspective, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE
)
performed_observed_slopes

performed_observed_slope_diffs <- pairs(performed_observed_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
performed_observed_slope_diffs

contrast(
  emtrends(performed_observed_trend, ~ condition * perspective, var = "effort_num"),
  interaction = c(condition = "revpairwise", perspective = "pairwise"),
  infer = TRUE
)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r performed-observed-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(performed_observed_slopes, performed_observed_slope_diffs,
              labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

```{r performed-observed-plot}
pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.4)
performed_observed_plot <-
  performed_observed_means %>%
  mutate(
    condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price"),
    point_fill = if_else(perspective == "Perform", as.character(condition), "Open")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = perspective, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3, position = pd) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = perspective), position = pd) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = point_fill), shape = 21, position = pd) +
  scale_evl(guide = "none", fill = TRUE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(Perform = "solid", Observe = "dashed"), name = "Perspective"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Liking and Price",
    subtitle = "Participating or Observing",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom") +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))

save_figure(performed_observed_plot, "performed_observed_ratings")
```

# Rating Profiles Across Experiments

Each experiment's analysis classifies every participant's ratings as
increasing or decreasing from low to high effort. This section pools those
participant-level classifications: the direction proportions per judgment
type in each experiment, and the crossed liking–price combinations for the
within-subjects design, the one case in which the same participant supplies
both judgments.

```{r profiles-experiments-data}
stepping_profile_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/stepping/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(subjID = as.factor(subjID),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value", "Wanting")))

observed_profile_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/observed/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(id = as.factor(id),
         scale_type = factor(scale_type, levels = c("Liking", "Value")))

clicking_within_profile_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/clicking_within/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(id = as.factor(id),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value")))

reveal_profile_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/main.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  filter(reveal_assignment == "progressive") %>%
  mutate(id = as.factor(id),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value")))

cognitive_profile_data <-
  bind_rows(
    read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/cogletters.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
    read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/subtractn.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(id = as.factor(id),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value")))

prices_within_profile_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/prices_within/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(id = as.factor(id),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Buyer", "Seller")))

clicking_within_profile_trends <- derive_effort_profiles(clicking_within_profile_data)

experiment_profiles <- bind_rows(
  derive_effort_profiles(stepping_profile_data, id = "subjID") %>%
    transmute(experiment = "Experiment 1 (Stepping)",
              judgment = recode(as.character(condition), Value = "Price"),
              profile),
  derive_effort_profiles(observed_profile_data, groups = "scale_type") %>%
    transmute(experiment = "Experiment 2 (Observed)",
              judgment = recode(as.character(scale_type), Value = "Price"),
              profile),
  clicking_within_profile_trends %>%
    transmute(experiment = "Experiment 3 (Clicking)",
              judgment = recode(as.character(condition), Value = "Price"),
              profile),
  derive_effort_profiles(reveal_profile_data) %>%
    transmute(experiment = "Experiment 4 (Reveal)",
              judgment = recode(as.character(condition), Value = "Price"),
              profile),
  derive_effort_profiles(cognitive_profile_data) %>%
    transmute(experiment = "Experiment 5 (Cognitive)",
              judgment = recode(as.character(condition), Value = "Price"),
              profile),
  derive_effort_profiles(prices_within_profile_data) %>%
    transmute(experiment = "Experiment 6B (Prices)",
              judgment = recode(as.character(condition),
                                Buyer = "Buying", Seller = "Selling"),
              profile)
) %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = c(
      "Experiment 1 (Stepping)", "Experiment 2 (Observed)",
      "Experiment 3 (Clicking)", "Experiment 4 (Reveal)",
      "Experiment 5 (Cognitive)", "Experiment 6B (Prices)"
    )),
    judgment = factor(judgment, levels = c("Liking", "Wanting", "Price",
                                           "Buying", "Selling")),
    profile = factor(profile, levels = c("Decreasing", "Increasing"))
  )
```

```{r profiles-experiments-summary}
experiment_profile_props <- experiment_profiles %>%

summarize_effort_profiles(experiment_profiles, groups = c("experiment", "judgment"))

experiment_profile_counts <- crossed_profile_counts(clicking_within_profile_trends)

experiment_profile_counts
```

# Instrumentality Across Experiments

The post-surveys of Experiments 3, 4, 5, 6B, and S7 included six items on how
participants had experienced their effort: whether it led to obtaining the
objects, whether it was necessary and worthwhile, whether the collecting task
and the effort itself were meaningful, and whether their actions served a
purpose. Each item was answered on a five-point scale scored so that a higher
value means more of the named quality, and Experiment S6 asked the same six
items about its waiting. This section describes the responses of each analyzed
sample, with Experiment 5 split by task.

```{r instrumentality-data}
instrumentality_items <- c(
  "Led to the objects" = "instrumental_task", "Necessary" = "necessary_effort",
  "Worthwhile" = "worthwhile_effort", "Meaningful task" = "meaning_task",
  "Meaningful effort" = "meaning_effort", "Served a purpose" = "actions_purpose"
)

instrumentality_reveal <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/main.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

instrumentality_cognitive <-
  bind_rows(
    read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/cogletters.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
    read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/subtractn.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

instrumentality_responses <- list(
  "Experiment 3" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/clicking_within/data/post.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
  "Experiment 4" =
    filter(instrumentality_reveal, reveal_assignment == "progressive"),
  "Experiment 5, letter transposition" =
    filter(instrumentality_cognitive, effort_task == "cogletters"),
  "Experiment 5, serial subtraction" =
    filter(instrumentality_cognitive, effort_task == "subtractn"),
  "Experiment 6B" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/prices_within/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment S6" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/wait/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment S7" =
    filter(instrumentality_reveal, reveal_assignment == "endpoint")
) %>%
  map(~ select(.x, all_of(instrumentality_items))) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "sample") %>%
  mutate(sample = fct_inorder(sample)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "item", values_to = "response") %>%
  mutate(item = factor(item, levels = names(instrumentality_items)))
```

The mean and standard deviation of each item summarize the level of each
sample's ratings.

```{r instrumentality-summary}
instrumentality_summary <- instrumentality_responses %>%
  group_by(sample, item) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(response), sd = sd(response), .groups = "drop")

instrumentality_summary %>%
  transmute(sample, n, item, m_sd = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean, sd)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = item, values_from = m_sd)
```

The percentage of participants choosing each scale point shows how the ratings
are distributed around those means.

```{r instrumentality-distribution}
instrumentality_responses %>%
  count(sample, item, response) %>%
  group_by(sample, item) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = response, values_from = percent,
              values_fill = 0, names_sort = TRUE)
```

# Post-Experiment Task Load Across Experiments

After the rating trials, participants in every main experiment and in
Experiments S6 and S7 rated the task on the NASA-TLX: mental, physical, and
temporal demand, performance, effort, and frustration, with pleasure as a
seventh component in the online surveys of Experiments 2, 3, 4, 5, 6B, S6, and
S7. The two laboratory experiments (1 and 6A) used the NASA-TLX application
and its 0–100 scale, the survey of Experiment 2 rated the effort participants
had observed on a slider from 1 to 20 with 11 positions, and the later surveys
used sliders from 0 to 20, so every component is expressed on the 0–100 metric
of the original instrument. Performance runs from "perfect" to "failure", so a
higher value means worse performance; the performance item of Experiment 2,
which asked how successful the observed person was, is reversed onto that
direction. This section describes the ratings of each analyzed sample.

```{r taskload-data}
taskload_components <- c(
  Mental = "tlx_mental", Physical = "tlx_physical", Temporal = "tlx_temporal",
  Performance = "tlx_performance", Effort = "tlx_effort",
  Frustration = "tlx_frustration", Pleasure = "tlx_pleasure"
)

taskload_reveal <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/main.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

taskload_cognitive <-
  bind_rows(
    read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/cogletters.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
    read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/subtractn.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

taskload_ratings <- list(
  "Experiment 1" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/stepping/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(subjID, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment 2 (observed)" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/observed/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment 3" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/clicking_within/data/post.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
  "Experiment 4" = filter(taskload_reveal, reveal_assignment == "progressive"),
  "Experiment 5, letter transposition" =
    filter(taskload_cognitive, effort_task == "cogletters"),
  "Experiment 5, serial subtraction" =
    filter(taskload_cognitive, effort_task == "subtractn"),
  "Experiment 6A" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/prices_between/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment 6B" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/prices_within/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment S6" =
    read_csv(here("experiments/wait/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
  "Experiment S7" = filter(taskload_reveal, reveal_assignment == "endpoint")
) %>%
  map(~ select(.x, all_of(taskload_components[names(taskload_components) != "Pleasure"]),
               any_of(taskload_components["Pleasure"]))) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "sample") %>%
  mutate(sample = fct_inorder(sample)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "component", values_to = "rating",
               values_drop_na = TRUE) %>%
  tlx_factor()
```

The mean and standard deviation of each component summarize each sample's
ratings, with a dash where a sample was not asked the component.

```{r taskload-summary}
taskload_summary <- taskload_ratings %>%
  group_by(sample, component) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(rating), sd = sd(rating), .groups = "drop")

taskload_summary %>%
  transmute(sample, n, component, m_sd = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean, sd)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = m_sd,
              values_fill = "—", names_sort = TRUE)
```

The means with their 95% confidence intervals place the samples side by side
within each component.

```{r taskload-plot}
teal <- evl_colours[["Teal"]]

taskload_plot <- taskload_summary %>%
  mutate(half_width = qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean, y = fct_rev(sample))) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = mean - half_width, xmax = mean + half_width),
                width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3, colour = teal, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(colour = teal) +
  facet_wrap(~component, nrow = 2, axes = "all_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = c(0, 50, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Rating (0–100)", y = NULL) +
  theme_evl(panel = c(30, 45))

show_figure(taskload_plot)
```

# Object Liking and the Effects of Effort

This exploratory check asks whether the Experiment 4 dissociation depends on
how much the objects are liked to begin with. Each object's liking is its mean
rating among the liking raters of Experiment S6, which showed the same 18
objects without effort; it enters the Experiment 4 trend model as a continuous
moderator, and the effort slopes are read one SD below and above its mean over
the rated trials.

```{r object-liking}
object_liking <-
  wait_data %>%
  filter(condition == "Liking") %>%
  group_by(img) %>%
  summarize(object_liking = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")

object_liking %>%
  summarize(n = n(), min = min(object_liking), max = max(object_liking),
            mean = mean(object_liking), sd = sd(object_liking))

reveal_object_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/main.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  filter(reveal_assignment == "progressive") %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  ) %>%
  left_join(object_liking, by = "img")

# Agreement with the same objects' mean liking in Experiment 4
reveal_object_data %>%
  filter(condition == "Liking") %>%
  group_by(img) %>%
  summarize(liking = mean(rating), object_liking = first(object_liking), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarize(r = cor(liking, object_liking))

object_liking_levels <-
  mean(reveal_object_data$object_liking) + c(-1, 1) * sd(reveal_object_data$object_liking)
object_liking_levels

object_liking_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition * object_liking + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_object_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)
nice(object_liking_trend)

object_liking_slopes <- emtrends(
  object_liking_trend, ~ condition | object_liking, var = "effort_num",
  at = list(object_liking = object_liking_levels), infer = TRUE
)
object_liking_slopes
pairs(object_liking_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
```

# Rating Response Time and the Effects of Effort

This exploratory check asks whether the Experiment 4 dissociation depends on
how quickly the judgments were made. Rating response time, log-transformed for
its right skew, enters the trend model as a continuous moderator, and the
dissociation is read one SD below and above its mean.

```{r rating-response-time}
reveal_rt_data <- mutate(reveal_object_data, log_rt = log(rt))

reveal_rt_data %>%
  summarize(n = n_distinct(id), ratings = n(), median_rt = median(rt))
reveal_rt_data %>%
  group_by(effort_level) %>%
  summarize(median_rt = median(rt))

log_rt_levels <- mean(reveal_rt_data$log_rt) + c(-1, 1) * sd(reveal_rt_data$log_rt)
exp(log_rt_levels)

rt_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition * log_rt + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_rt_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)
nice(rt_trend)

pairs(
  emtrends(rt_trend, ~ condition | log_rt, var = "effort_num",
           at = list(log_rt = log_rt_levels), infer = TRUE),
  infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE
)
```

# Summary

Experiments S5 and S6 test the dissociation with the same two effort slopes and
their difference, Δb, as the main experiments do, and the table gathers those
with the sample sizes of Experiments S1 to S4 and of the pooled comparison of
performed and observed effort. As in the main notebook, the summary file also
carries each slope as a standardized effect, d.

```{r summary}
supplementary_summary <- bind_rows(
  key_result("Experiment S1", "Experiment S1: Laboratory Stepping", n_taskload_stepping),
  key_result("Experiment S2", "Experiment S2: Online Clicking", n_taskload_clicking),
  key_result("Experiment S3", "Experiment S3: Price and Liking at Baseline", n_price_liking_analyzed),
  key_result("Experiment S4", "Experiment S4: Explicit Price and Liking", n_price_magnitude),
  key_result("Experiment S5", "Experiment S5: Foraging Experience", n_foraging,
             foraging_slopes, foraging_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = foraging_trend),
  key_result("Experiment S6", "Experiment S6: Waiting", n_wait,
             wait_slopes, wait_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = wait_trend),
  key_result("Performed vs observed effort", "Performed vs Observed Effort", n_performed_observed)
)

supplementary_summary %>%
  transmute(
    study, n,
    falls = if_else(is.na(delta), "", sprintf("%s: %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", falls, falls_b, falls_lower, falls_upper)),
    rises = if_else(is.na(delta), "", sprintf("%s: %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", rises, rises_b, rises_lower, rises_upper)),
    difference = if_else(is.na(delta), "", sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f], t(%.0f) = %.2f",
                                                   delta, delta_lower, delta_upper, delta_df, delta_t))
  )

write_csv(supplementary_summary, here("output/key_results_supplementary.csv"))
```
